title: California Roofing: AB 888, 10% coverage, and more
summary: Class A, AB 888 (Safe Homes), and 10% update coverage have changed the game for roofers in California. Here’s how to educate homeowners and win work in 2027.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


California rewrote the rulebook on fire-safe roofing in 2026 and many homeowners don't know it yet. Between AB 888 and the new insurance mandate, roofing contractors who know their stuff will be best positioned to help homeowners with their reroofing projects in 2027.


Roofing contractors in California: two significant changes hit California homeowners this year. Understanding both of them, and being able to explain them clearly, is one of the fastest ways to turn a conversation into a signed contract.


Here’s how to adapt, educate homeowners, and win more work heading into 2027.


**By the way: for a quick reference on everything you'll need to know, download the free PDF resource at the end of this article.**


## **Class A Roofing**


As of January 1, 2026, a **Class A fire-rated roof** is required by law in[Fire Hazard Severity Zones](https://osfm.fire.ca.gov/what-we-do/community-wildfire-preparedness-and-mitigation/fire-hazard-severity-zones) .


- Non-compliant materials, like wood shake or cedar shingles, will fail inspection.
- Most carriers now require documented Class A roofing in high-risk areas.


California’s FAIR Plan (insurer of last resort) just[announced a rate hike](https://www.kqed.org/news/12094860/california-fair-plan-announces-29-1-rate-hike-for-homeowners-this-fall) , so affected homeowners want to find private coverage ASAP. A Class A roof can make that happen.


## **AB 888**


The[California Safe Homes](https://calmatters.digitaldemocracy.org/bills/ca_202520260ab888) (AB 888) state grant program also passed into law on Jan 1, 2026.


- Helps income-qualified homeowners in high-risk areas afford fire-safe roof updates.
- For now (Oct 2026), there’s[no application portal, no waitlist, and no launch info yet](https://readyfireone.com/learn/articles/california-home-hardening-grants) .


Once those grants come through, qualified homeowners will be lining up for roof work. Until then, they may qualify for a[Safer from Wildfires insurance discount](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/01-consumers/200-wrr/Safer-from-Wildfires.cfm) with that Class A roof.


## **10% Update Coverage Mandate**


Here’s the most exciting one. As of July 1, 2026, new or renewed insurance policies must now include[building code upgrade coverage](https://insuranceclaimsinfo.com/resources/new-california-insurance-laws-2025-2026) **of at least 10% of the dwelling limit** .


- Insurers pay the difference between repairing to the old standard and rebuilding to fire code.
- Until now, many homeowners didn't have this coverage, or had caps too low to matter.


Here’s an example. If a homeowner has a $500,000 dwelling limit, their insurer’s now on the hook for $50,000 to bring a damaged roof up to code (including those Class A materials). That’s a lot of homeowners who can now afford roofing projects, whether they know it or not.


## **What to Tell Homeowners**


Homeowners rely on you, their neighborhood roofer, to help guide, inform, and protect them. Break it down or send them this summary so they understand their options.


**"Your insurance is paying for this."** The 10% code upgrade coverage means the insurer covers the cost of bringing a roof up to Class A. Homeowners don’t pay that out of pocket.


**"You’ll need a compliant roof to keep your coverage."** In high-risk zones, an undocumented or non-compliant roof can be a reason for non-renewal. Get those Class A materials on file.


**"There may be grant funding coming."** For income-qualified homeowners in fire hazard zones, AB 888 will be huge. Hopefully, the Department of Insurance[will share more info soon](https://www.insurance.ca.gov/0400-news/0102-alerts/index.cfm) .


**"I'll document everything for your insurer."** A compliant install with proper permits, material documentation, and photos means no stress later.
